From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Optimize credits & quantization — packaging and credit-commit options

Hi Susan —

Great to meet last week. I promised a concise follow-up on how Redwood's Optimize toolkit can be packaged for Quantica's inference workloads and the pricing shapes we typically offer. Quick summary up front:

- Optimize is sold as an add-on credit pack (monthly or annual commit) that applies to savings features (batching/caching) and includes a consult for quantization recommendations.
- Typical commercial levers: committed credits (lower $/token), multi-month discounts, and a small professional services block for model profiling.

Attached is a short pricing summary and one-pager (redwood_optimize_pricing_v2.pdf) with three starter packs we recommend for customers at your scale. A few answers to questions you mentioned:

1) Do cache hits reduce billing?
   - Yes — for prefix/KV cache hits Redwood can reduce billable tokens (we meter based on emitted tokens plus a small charge for cached KV retrieval depending on policy). We can show a modeled impact once we profile your request distribution.

2) What quantization levels are recommended?
   - We surface recommendations per-model and per-prompt. In production we often recommend int8 for a safe accuracy/cost tradeoff; int4 is available on select model variants with an experimental support flag and needs per-prompt evals due to accuracy delta. Optimize includes eval tooling to validate.

3) How do discounts scale with commit size?
   - We provide incremental discounts at 6-, 12-, and 24-month commitments. For a ballpark, a 12-month commit for a mid-size customer usually nets ~15% off listed credit pricing, plus operational credits against onboarding. Exact bands are in the attached.

Next steps: If you and procurement can share a rough annual credit target (tokens/embeddings), I can run a modeled proposal and send a draft SOW. Would you prefer monthly or annual invoicing?

Thanks — looking forward to making this simple for your infra team.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Susan —

Good questions. Short answers, then a suggested next step.

- Metering & caching: we bill emitted tokens plus a small per-request KV access surcharge for cache misses. For a 30% prefix hit-rate you should see ~20–25% reduction in billable token volume for typical generation mixes (exact depends on average generation length). The pricing sheet includes a worked example — happy to run your traffic through our profiler for a precise model.

- Int4 in production: we have customers in non-regulated workloads running int4 for specific Llama-family variants with minor accuracy drift on non-critical prompts. For regulated health use-cases we typically recommend int8 as the default, then use Optimize's eval harness to validate any int4 candidate on your test prompts.

- Commercial: 20% is at the high end for a first-year ask on credit list price. Typical outcomes we’ve seen: 12-month commits land in the 12–18% range depending on the size of the commit and additional operational concessions (onboarding credits, extended support).

I’ve attached a slightly revised pricing sheet with an example 12-month commit scenario and three commitment bands. If you like, I can convert the mid-band into a modeled proposal using your estimated token volumes. Let me know who from procurement I should loop in.

Best,
Priyom
[Attachment: redwood_optimize_pricing_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)]

Thanks for the thread. Quick internal play: Quantica is asking for 20% on a $120k 12-month commit. Given the size and the fact this is a new account in a regulated vertical, I recommend we offer 18% off list on the credit pack plus:

- Two months of onboarding support (no-cost) to run the Optimize profiling and the initial evals for int4 candidates.
- One-time operational credit of $7,500 applied against the first invoice to cover SRE/infra assistance.
- Standard 30-day termination with annual true-up clause (they commit to spend but can true-up if usage is lower).

Rationale: keeps concessions limited, gives them operational runway to prove int4 candidates without more pricing give, and preserves margin. If they push back hard on 20% we can escalate an extra 1–2% (to 19%) with a shorter onboarding credit.

If you want, I can draft the SOW language and the pricing line items for procurement.
